. mission sunday 2026: one in christ, united in mission. domhnach na misean. as we celebrate the centenary of world mission day, established by pope pius xi (1926), pope leo xiv invites us to reflect in his message for the 100th world mission day on the theme “one in christ, united in mission ”: 1. one in christ: pope leo reminds us that the church must “renew and sustain spiritual and fraternal unity ”. in a world marked by division and mistrust, our wit- ness requires “hearts that are reconciled and eager for communion ”. unity in christ is the foundation of our missionary calling. 2. united in mission: mission belongs to every baptised person: “no baptized person is exempt from or indifferent to mission ”. as pope leo emphasises, pro- claiming the gospel “is an action that is always harmonious, communal and syn- odal”. called to walk together, we must listen, share our gifts, embrace diversity and work together so that the world may believe in christ. 3. mission to love: “if unity is the condition of mission, love is its essence ”. our mission is to make god’s faithful love visible through our words, actions and ser- vice, for the church’s mission is “born of love, lived in love, and leading to love ”. we also remember with gratitude missionaries who bring christ’s love to commu- nities across the world, often amid great challenges and conflicts. today's mission sunday collection goes to missio ireland, part of the world- wide pontifical mission societies, the pope’s official charity for overseas mis- sions particularly in asia, latin america and africa. evening prayer for fr willie doyle. the parish is warmly invited to join in evening prayer (vespers) in the cathedral of christ the king, mullingar, on this sunday, 18 october 2026 at 4.00pm , marking an important moment in the cause for the canonisation of fr willie doyle sj. fr willie doyle was an irish jesuit priest who served as a chaplain to the british army during the first world war. he gave his life ministering to wounded and dying soldiers during the battle of passchendaele in 1917. his reputation for holiness has remained strong, and in 2022 bishop tom opened the diocesan tribunal for the cause of his can- onisation, with the approval of the holy see. the diocesan investigation has now reached its conclusion. following the celebration of vespers, the public conclud- ing session of the tribunal will take place in the cathedral. this is a si gnificant occasion for the diocese and for all who have a devotion to fr willie doyle. it will be the first diocesan tribunal to conclude in ireland for over forty years. fol- lowing the ceremony, the documentation gathered during the investigation will be sent to the dicastery for the causes of saints in rome. all are very welcome to join us for this special celebration of evening prayer and to pray for the con- tinued progress of fr willie doyle’s cause. cathedral closing nightly at 8 pm. vocations to priesthood: are you considering becoming a priest in the diocese of meath? vocations holy hour. st cianán’s church, duleek, co meath. friday 23rd october 7pm. live from facebook page: diocese of meath vocations. vocations contact the experience of fragility raises the question of whether we are able to remain close to one another when life no longer corresponds to what had been hoped for, and whether we can recognise the work of grace even in situations marked by limits, wounds and apparent failure. in this respect too, the experience of families has something to teach everyone , since fragility belongs to our common human condition and therefore also to the life of the church. we all know the gap between the good we desire and what we are able to live. we need grace, forgiveness and new beginnings to accomplish god’s will, and learn that fidelity is itself a grace to be received and a path to be gradually renewed, often through trial. recognizing this shared challenge should shape the way we accompany one another in the church. what kind of church, then, do people encounter precisely when they are most fragile? do our communities help them discover that they still have a place, a responsibility and gifts to offer? can the truth we proclaim be encountered through the patience, closeness and mercy of our pastoral presence? how can we announce to them the fullness of the gospel’s teaching about the family? pope leo xiv, “proclaiming the gospel with families today”, 7th october 2026 twenty - ninth week in ordinary time 18 - 24 oct 2026 saturday: st. mary’s 6pm dairina byrne, st brigid’s villas ( month’s mind ) sunday: st. oliver’s 12noon john sherlock , rathaldron ( month’s mind ) st. mary’s 1pm oliver halpin , aylesbury lodge ( month’s mind ) saturday st mary’s 10am anniversaries occurring brian alexander james maher maggie mcdonagh michael & teresa boland né sharkey jimmy & bridie coogan & decmem coogan fam jack skelly jim monaghan (2 ) johnny gavin annie & danny quinn sheila & finn owens mona conway ken harte may & eileen harte mary brennan mary & anthony farrell & decmem farrell fam james, josephine, hilary, miriam & seamus brady patrick & helen healy josie geoghegan camillus geoghegan patrick bird michel cullen catherine knox marcella cahill bernadette donag hy joseph donaghy olive thompson angela garbutt florence lawless mary curley dermot & mollie cuffe gr áinne windle né cuffe paddy callinan paddy & annie smith marie lynch colette horton & all holy souls who have nobody to remember or to pray for them by name. kindly provide names for saturday anniversaries at least ten days in advance for inclusion in the parish bulletin saturday: st. mary’s 6pm anne ‘nancy’ blake , commons road ( first ann ) sunday: st. anne’s 2pm african community mass requested conrad sharkey james, brena , pauline, brena & marie lanney paddy, elaine & noel woods hannah earley alan murtagh mary lawless thanks to parishioners for your recent generosity. offertory: €5,470 development fund: €2,411 collection for the support and care of retired pri ests: €5,845 st mary’s cemetery summer: monday - saturday: 2pm - 9pm; sunday: 9am - 9pm

come and �nd peace in the lord. also on the first saturday of every month- devotions in clara church at 2.55pm. everyone welcome to attend. join us for evena brief period of time. give back to caesar what belongs to caesar. what is important for us who live in today’s world is this: jesus always was a broad-minded and open p erson. nowhere in the gospels can we find even a hint of narrow-mindedness. he had friends who were pharisees and friends wh o were tax-collectors and lepers and samaritans. jesus always refused to enter into narrow, dualistic thinking. he did not in habit an ‘either/or’ world, and he was always broadminded and balanced. and, as christians, we are called to be the same. this is much more difficult than we might think! also, we live within the kingdoms of this world, and we can often feel battered, bruised and disillusioned by the lifestyles, politics and values of these kingdoms. i n today’s gospel jesus reassures us that this is ok . we live within the kingdoms of this world and it is morally correct to support them in so far as we have to, but (and this is cruci al) our allegiance, our loyalty and the way we live our lives must always be to the kingdom of god. jesus warns of hypocrisy – calling ourselves citizens of god’s kingdom and its currency of love, whiles upporting or condoning the currency of the kingdoms of this world – injusti ce, judgement, intolerance, sarcasm, violence, fear. the re is so much to learn from today’s gospel which is relevant to us and our place in our world. it certainly gives us plenty to reflect upon… collections 10th/11th october – development fund: €1,425 ; plate: €7 45 ; october offerings: €1,395 . thank you very much! closing of the diocesan inquiry into the cause for the beatification and canonization of fr william doyle sj will take place in the cathedral of christ the king, mullingar, at 4.00pm this sunday 18th october. the celebration will begin with solemn vespers , presided over by bishop deenihan with the homily given by fr. conor mcdonough op . evening prayer will be sung by the mullingar cathedral choir, cathedral choristers and the meath diocesan choir, before the formal closing session of the inquiry. all are welcome. pope leo xiv has written this prayer to mark the 100th anniversary of world mission sunday. holy father, make us one in christ, rooted in his love that unites and renews. may all members of the church be united in mission, docile to the holy spirit, courageous in bearing witness to the gospel, proclaiming and embodying daily your faithful love for all creatures. bless all missionary men and women, support them in their efforts, and watch over them in hope! mary, queen of missions, accompany our work of evangelisation in every corner of t he earth: make us instruments of peace, and grant that the whole world may recognise in christ the light that saves. amen. the next meeting of the parish pastoral council (ppc) is at 7.30 p in the parochial house on tuesday, 20th october.
